CheckTitle: Amplify app and branch environment variables do not contain secrets
CheckType: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Description: AWS Amplify app and branch environment variables are inspected for values that resemble secrets, such as API keys, passwords, tokens, and connection strings. Findings identify the variable name and detector type without exposing the secret value.
Risk: Secrets stored in Amplify environment variables can be read by users or automation with configuration access and may be exposed through build logs, frontend builds, or compromised CI/CD workflows. Exposed credentials can enable unauthorized access, data exfiltration, and application tampering.

Code.NativeIaC:
```yaml
Resources:
  <example_resource_name>:
    Type: AWS::Amplify::App
    Properties:
      EnvironmentVariables:
        - Name: <NON_SECRET_CONFIGURATION_NAME>
          Value: <non_secret_value>
```
Code.Other:
1. Open the AWS Amplify console and select the affected app or branch
2. Review Environment variables
3. Remove secrets from app-level and branch-level variables
4. Store secrets in AWS Secrets Manager or AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store and retrieve them through a secure backend workflow instead of exposing them to Amplify builds or frontend code
5. Rotate any credential that may have been exposed

Recommendation.Text: Do not store secrets directly in Amplify app or branch environment variables. Use AWS Secrets Manager or Systems Manager Parameter Store through backend services, keep frontend configuration non-sensitive, restrict configuration read access, and rotate any exposed credentials.
